headline: Majors hold above 200-day lines with RSI overbought across the board; whales withdrew $108M from Kraken overnight while ETF inflows persist unevenly
paragraphs: The regime is bullish on structure: all seven assets sit above their 200-day simple moving average, and none have crossed above it yet (golden_cross remains false everywhere). This is the foundation. Against that foundation, momentum tells a different story. Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, and BNB all carry RSI-14 readings between 68.8 and 74.8, which is overbought territory by the classical measure. ADA sits lower at 52.2 with MACD below its signal line, a clean reversal signal, while the other six carry MACD above signal, which aligns with the uptrend. The tension here is real: trend is intact but momentum is stretched. When RSI stays this high for this long without a pullback, either the move has further fuel or it is setting up a mean-reversion flush. MACD still points up, so acceleration remains possible, but the room for extension without a rest is narrowing.

Positioning in derivatives shows crowding on the long side across all the majors. Bitcoin has a 1.23 long-to-short ratio at $2.2 billion open interest, Ethereum sits at 1.42 ratio with $1.5 billion open, and Solana is aggressively long at 1.67 ratio with $336 million OI. XRP pushes to 2.49 long-to-short, and Doge is the extreme: 3.99 longs per short with only $89 million open interest. Funding rates are the cost of holding these positions. Bitcoin and Ethereum carry modest rates (2.8% and 1.8% annualized), well within normal range; XRP sits at 3.7%, also manageable. But Solana is paying shorts, with funding at negative 8.7% annualized, and Doge is expensive for longs at 6.6% annualized. That negative Solana rate is a relief valve: when shorts are being paid to hold, the long-side crowding has less runway before pain. Liquidations over the past 21-23 hours show shorts taking the heavy losses (Bitcoin shorts: $779k liquidated against $117k longs; Ethereum shorts: $774k against $111k longs), which is consistent with a bull move, but the size is not enormous relative to the open interest, suggesting the squeeze is steady rather than violent.

Flows present a contradiction worth naming. Over the last five trading sessions, Bitcoin ETF inflows sum to $924.5 million net positive. Yet on August 28, the latest daily print, Bitcoin spot ETFs recorded an outflow of $201.9 million. This disagreement means that four of the previous five days carried large inflows that offset one bad day. Ethereum, by contrast, shows agreement: the latest day on August 28 was a $102.1 million inflow, and the five-session sum is $815.7 million, all in the same direction. Stablecoin float stands at $309.8 billion, up 1.11% over the past month, which is modest accumulation of dry powder. Neither a buildup nor a drawdown. The real tell came off-exchange: over the past 24 hours, $108.4 million in Bitcoin moved off Kraken into self-custody, the single largest whale move in the data. This is the first time in three weeks that whales moved coins away from the bid. The prior three weekly windows show the opposite: week ending August 16 had $508 million moving onto exchanges, week ending August 23 had $1.062 billion onto exchanges, and week ending August 30 still shows $659 million onto exchanges. That trend is reversing, at least in this snapshot. Whales began moving coins off just as spot ETF inflows hit a speed bump.

Sentiment sits at 69 on the Fear & Greed gauge, firmly in Greed territory, and the 30-day range has been 25 to 74, so today is neither the extreme high nor a retest of extremes. This is a garden-variety greed state, the kind that can persist for weeks. The tape does not match the sentiment. Overbought momentum (RSI 70+), long-side crowding in derivatives, and whales quietly moving coins to cold storage while one day's ETF inflows turned negative are not the fingerprints of a market confident in going higher. They look like a market priced for a move already partially complete, with conviction fraying at the edges. The price action on the day itself is flat to slightly red (Bitcoin down 0.1%, Solana down 0.3%, XRP down 0.3%), which on a 20% month is a shrug, but after a 7% week it is the first serious pause.

Distance from the 12-month highs deserves a glance. Bitcoin sits 37.4% below its all-time high of $124,740, Ethereum is 47.8% below $4,707, Solana is 57.5% below $247.60, and ADA is the worst at 78.4% below $0.930. These are not fresh all-time highs; they are legit pullbacks from previous peaks. The market has recovered into a strong trend, but it has not erased the damage from the prior cycle top. That context matters: when you are 37% to 78% off the high and momentum is overbought, the directional opportunity is narrower than the headlines suggest.

Watch for a break of the 200-day simple moving average on any major, which would signal a regime shift. Watch for Solana's funding rate: if it stays negative and long-side open interest expands, that is evidence of desperation, a warning flag. Watch Bitcoin whale flows and ETF inflows: if the off-exchange withdrawal continues while spot inflows turn negative for a second or third day, that would be the first sign that the smart money and the traditional bid are diverging. Finally, watch RSI: a drop from 70+ back into the 50-60 band without a price collapse would be the kind of healthy pullback that keeps a trend alive. The chart shows strength, but it also shows fatigue. The next few sessions will show which one wins.
